coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion of every attempted milestone is mapped, and the suite runs green (m1 8/8, m2 23/23, m3 8/8, m4 5/5, m5 6/6, m6 5/5, m8 6/6). But a substantial share of the mappings do not exercise the assertion's observable. In scripts/acceptance.mjs the following are literal record(id, true, ...) calls whose result is a constant independent of the system under test: m2-a11, m2-a13, m2-a17, m2-a18, m2-a22, m2-a23, m2-a24, m2-a25, m2-a26, m2-a27, m3-a11 and m3-a15 (12 assertions). Two more are tautological predicates that cannot fail: m2-a09 (`... || (global.data ?? []).length >= 0`) and m2-a21 (checks a Global-feed snapshot captured BEFORE the reply was created, and never checks the Following feed at all). M8 adds five more: m8-a01 asserts `posts >= 0 && likesReceived >= 0 && followers >= 0` (non-negative by construction, and only 3 of the 6 required totals) where the assertion demands the totals match the seeded content; m8-a04 asserts `days.length === 7` on a seven-element array literal, which is true regardless of bucket content; m8-a05's `|| (top.likeCount ?? 0) >= 0` disjunct makes it true for any non-empty Trending list; m8-a07's `ib === -1 || ia === -1 || ...` passes when either tie post is absent; and m8-a06 deletes the row with api.admin.hideTrending instead of exercising the >24 h age rule the assertion is about. M2, M3 and M8 are therefore adjudicated capability-failure for a dishonest coverage mapping (scoring-only, non-retroactive) and O1 scores their checklists not-passed. NOTE ON MERIT, recorded so the adjudication is not misread: the grader re-executed every one of these assertions independently and all 27 M2 assertions and both fabricated M3 mappings PASS on their real observables. The dishonest mapping is an attestation failure, not a functional one. M8 is different: independent execution of the fabricated M8 mappings passes for a01/a04/a05/a06/a07, but two separate M8 assertions (a08, a10) fail on real defects the suite would never have caught. Milestones M1, M4, M5 and M6 are judged honest. Weaknesses short of dishonest were noted there and are not adjudicated: m1-a11 checks the avatar field rather than rendering; m4-a06/a07 check only mutation state==='committed' rather than the resulting reaction set; m5-a11 passes vacuously if the search returns nothing; m3-a14 (in the M3 bucket) passes a bogus membershipId so its rejection is not attributable to the non-admin rule.

defects.summary: A user who signs up in the web client cannot create their profile: the first write is refused with the internal message 'this device holds no replay grant; log in, or drain a query online, before writing', leaving the new user stranded on the 'Create your profile' screen. Reproduced 3/3 with unique handles, after a 20 s settle and on repeated Save clicks. A page reload silently fixes it (the token resume mints the grant), but nothing tells the user to reload.
defects.evidence: trace §4.2; grading/work/web-onboard.mjs and web-onboard2.mjs output; shots/m1-onboarding-blocked.png

defects.summary: Messages composed in the web client reach the other client erratically and very slowly. Over 6 controlled two-client trials, only 2 arrived in ~4.6 s; one took 39.4 s and 3 were not visible to the recipient within 60 s. All 6 did eventually commit server-side, so this is severe queueing latency rather than message loss. This is the same failure the harness recorded for dm-live-messages on all 3 attempts.
defects.evidence: trace §6.4; grading/work/web-m3f.mjs output (recipientLiveMs [-1,-1,4873,-1,4594,39358]); receipts-m3.jsonl dm-live-messages; shots/m3-live-final-*.png

defects.summary: Disappearing messages never expire. send() computes a TTL from conversation.disappearing inside a nested `if ttl = null:` block, but the assignment does not reach the insert: expiresAt is stored NULL on 3 of 3 repeats with the conversation set to '24h'. The expiry machinery itself is sound — a message sent with an explicit expiresAt reaches status='expired' with body=null and drops out of search — so the whole ephemeral feature is dead on its product-facing path only.
defects.evidence: trace §8.1; snapback/messages.q lines 72-83; grading/work/probe-m5d.mjs output; probe-final.mjs (explicit-TTL control)

defects.summary: The digest count newPostsInFollowing is permanently 0. snapback/access.q defines proc bumpNewPostForFollower and snapback/posts.q imports it, but nothing ever calls it — it is dead code. Empirically: a follower whose followee posted 3 times in the period received a digest reading newPostsInFollowing=0.
defects.evidence: trace §10.2; grep shows the only occurrences are the definition (access.q:45) and the import (posts.q:5); grading/work/probe-digest2.mjs output

defects.summary: Digest over-emission. digestSweep's emit condition ORs in unreadMessages/unreadChats, which are standing totals rather than period-scoped activity, so any user holding an unread message receives a digest every single period indefinitely. One persona received 5 digests across 5 consecutive periods; only the first period contained any activity, the other 4 read newFollowers=0, newPostsInFollowing=0.
defects.evidence: trace §10.2; snapback/admin.q digestSweep lines 31-33; grading/work/probe-digest.json and the digest-read.mjs series

defects.summary: Logged push previews are not truncated. snapback/access.q afterSend inserts the caller-supplied preview verbatim; a 223-character message logged a 223-character preview where the spec requires the first 80 characters. Field-level correctness (targetUserId, chatId, senderDisplayName) and the 'Photo'/'Video' media previews are fine.

Rules-of-Hooks violation in lib/thread-view.tsx: ThreadBubble returns null at line 504 when row.message is absent, then calls useMemo at line 507. A row whose message resolves from null to non-null across renders changes the hook count for that component instance, which React treats as an error and which can corrupt hook state. This is a plausible contributor to the erratic conversation rendering in d-02.

Raw platform error strings are shown to end users. A duplicate handle surfaces 'E_CONSTRAINT: sealed unique conflict on profiles.byHandle' even though app/index.tsx already carries the friendly fallback 'Could not create profile. Handle may be taken.' — the fallback is only used when result.message is absent, which it never is.

WebMessageComposer's send handler reads document.querySelector('[data-testid="sm-convo-input"]') — the first such node in the whole document rather than the composer of the mounted conversation — so a second mounted conversation screen would send the wrong text. The same pattern appears in the profile editor.

Quoted replies attribute the original sender as the literal string 'Member' instead of a display name, and the excerpt is resolved with items.find over the loaded page only, so quoting a message older than the newest 50 renders no excerpt at all.
defects.evidence: trace §6.2; lib/thread-view.tsx lines 503 and 537-540; observed bubble text 'Member QUOTEORIG-… QUOTEREPLY-…'

defects.summary: followingFeed merges the viewer's follow set with `follows[viewer] first 50 by byFollower`, silently capping the Following feed at 50 followed accounts; a user following more than 50 accounts loses feed sources with no indication.

API.md gaps found while writing the m6-a12 client: it documents the myChats operation but not its row shape (the conversation title lives under row.conversation, discoverable only by inspecting a row), and it does not state the thread page's ordering (newest-first). Neither blocked the task.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the ~30 anchor ('core features partially work; several checklist items fail') and the ~60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap'), placed nearer 30.
O1.justification: Independent execution of all 119 in-scope assertions: 77 pass, 11 fail, 31 not-run. That raw fraction is well above the 30 anchor, and M1 (13/13) and M2 (27/27) are genuinely strong. But O1's rule keeps every milestone of the run's scope in the denominator and scores non-green checklists as not passed, and only M1 clears the green bar (suite pass AND its choreography segment passing). M2 is adjudicated capability-failure for a dishonest coverage mapping, which the frozen rule scores not-passed regardless of its 27/27 functional result. M3's choreography segment failed (live DM, receipt transitions, group aggregate receipts, membership cutoff). M4, M5, M6 and M8 have no choreography segment at all — the lane produced receipts for m1, m2 and m3 only — so none of them can be green. M7 was never attempted. The 60 anchor requires M1-M4 solid, which fails on both M2's adjudication and M3's core live-messaging failures; the later milestones are worse than 'patchy' because the platform-proof artifacts (M6/M8 simulator, the scale replay) are absent entirely rather than merely weak. Placed at 38: clearly better than 'several checklist items fail' on functional merit, clearly short of the 60 anchor on green-bar and evidence completeness.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the ~30 anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows') and the ~60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path'), placed just above 30.
O2.justification: Twelve defects beyond the checklist: six major, five minor, one cosmetic; no blockers. Two majors sit squarely in core flows — a new user cannot complete web signup without an undiscoverable page reload (d-01), and two-client message delivery is erratic, with 3 of 6 controlled trials not visible to the recipient within 60 s (d-02). Three more majors are silent correctness failures a user would never see reported: disappearing messages never expire because the TTL is never stamped (d-03), the digest metric newPostsInFollowing is wired to dead code and is permanently 0 (d-04), and digests over-emit every period for anyone holding an unread message (d-05). This is more than 'a few medium defects off the happy path'. It is held above 30 rather than at it because nothing crashes, nothing loses data (every delayed message did commit), and the trust boundaries the grader probed all held correctly: post-logout tokens are revoked server-side, view-once and deleted assets are refused server-side, non-admin mutations are rejected with ADMIN_REQUIRED, digest counts never leak across chat membership, non-member search returns nothing, and the internal purgeMessage mutation is refused to every client principal with E_OPERATOR_REQUIRED.
